questions.question: For a function $f\colon A\to B$ and a subset $S\subseteq A$, what is the restriction $f|_S$?
options: The map $S\to f(S)$ obtained by shrinking both domain and codomain
A new rule on $S$, chosen so that its values lie in $S$
The map $A\to B$ that equals $f$ on $S$ and $0$ elsewhere

questions.question: What is the image of the restriction $f|_S$ of $f\colon A\to B$ to $S\subseteq A$?
options: $f(S)$, the set of values $f(x)$ with $x\in S$
$f(A)$, the image of $f$ on its whole domain

questions.question: Can a function that is not injective on its original domain become injective after restriction?
options: No: every collision remains after the domain is restricted
Yes: squaring on $\mathbb R$ becomes injective on $[0,\infty)$
Yes: every restriction to a proper subset is injective
No: injectivity requires changing the function's rule

questions.question: Can a real-valued function $f$ on a domain $A$ have no maximum on $A$, while its restriction to a subset $S\subseteq A$ has a maximum?
options: No: restriction preserves whether a maximum exists
Only if $f$ is bounded above on its original domain
Only if $S$ contains an interior stationary point
Yes: $f(x)=x$ on $\mathbb R$ has a maximum on $[0,1]$

questions.question: Let $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be given by $f(x)=x^2$. Which of the following maps is surjective?

Let $f\colon\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ be $f(x,y)=x+y$ and let $S=\{(x,y):x^2+y^2=1\}$. Using the parametrisation $p(t)=(\cos t,\sin t)$ for $t\in[0,2\pi]$, which formula gives $\varphi(t)=(f|_S)(p(t))$?
What is the maximum value of $f(x,y)=3x+4y$ restricted to the circle $x^2+y^2=1$?
For $f(x)=x^2$, on which set $S$ is the restriction $f|_S$ injective?
For $f(x)=x^2$ and $S=[-1,2]$, what is the image $f(S)$ of the restriction $f|_S$?
Let $f\colon A\to\mathbb R$ and $S\subseteq A$. Suppose $f$ attains a maximum on both $A$ and $S$. Which comparison always holds?
options: No comparison holds for all such $f$, $A$ and $S$

questions.question: Let $f\colon A\to B$, let $S\subseteq A$, and let $\iota\colon S\to A$ be the inclusion map $\iota(x)=x$. Which identity expresses restriction for every such function and subset?
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, let $f\colon A\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and let $S\subseteq A$. With continuity understood relative to each domain, what can be said about $f|_S$?
options: It may fail to be continuous at boundary points of $S$
It is continuous only when $S$ is open in $\mathbb R^n$
It is continuous only when $S$ is closed in $\mathbb R^n$

questions.question: Let $f\colon\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable and let $S=\{(x,y):x^2+y^2=1\}$. What can be said about $\nabla f$ at a maximiser of $f|_S$?
options: It is normal to the circle and need not be zero
It must be zero, as at an unconstrained interior maximum
It must be nonzero and tangent to the circle
It may be nonzero only when $f$ is linear

questions.question: What is the minimum of $f(x,y)=x^2+y^2$ restricted to the line $x+y=1$?
Let $f\colon(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be $f(x)=1/x$ and let $S=(1,2]$. What can be said about the maximum of $f|_S$?
options: The included endpoint $x=2$ gives the maximum $1/2$
There is no maximum because the values are unbounded above
There is no maximum; the supremum is $1$

questions.question: Let $f\colon\mathbb R\to[0,\infty)$ be $f(x)=(x-1)^2$ and let $g=f|_{(-\infty,1]}$. Which formula gives the inverse $g^{-1}(y)$ for $y\ge0$?
options: No inverse exists because $g$ is not injective

questions.question: Let $f\colon A\to B$ and suppose $A=S\cup T$, where $S$ and $T$ are nonempty disjoint subsets. Both restrictions $f|_S$ and $f|_T$ are injective. Which additional condition is necessary and sufficient for $f$ to be injective on $A$?

Let $f\colon A\to\mathbb R$ be $f(x,y)=1/(x-y)$, where $A=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x\ne y\}$. Let $C=\{(x,y):x^2+y^2=1\}$. What is the largest subset $S\subseteq C$ on which a restriction of this specified function is defined?
options: $S=C$: every point of the circle lies in $A$

questions.question: What are the maximum and minimum of $f(x,y)=xy$ restricted to the circle $x^2+y^2=1$?
options: None, as $xy$ has a saddle at the origin

questions.question: Let $f\colon\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ be $f(x,y)=x^2-y^2$. Restrict $f$ separately to the curves $C_1=\{(x,y):y=x-x^3\}$ and $C_2=\{(x,y):y=x+x^3\}$. How is the origin classified locally on $C_1$ and $C_2$, respectively?
options: A saddle point; a saddle point
A strict local minimum; a strict local minimum
No local extremum; no local extremum
A strict local minimum; a strict local maximum
